description: Research questions over the sample corpus. Automatic checks per answer: citation coverage (share of factual sentences with a [n]), citation validity (cited quote occurs verbatim in the cited chunk), whether the answer explicitly admits gaps, and an LLM-as-judge faithfulness score against the cited excerpts only. `expect_gap` marks questions the corpus cannot fully answer; a good answer says so.

questions.question: How does Raft elect a leader, and what prevents two leaders in the same term?
Compare Raft and Paxos: their roles, how a leader is chosen, and how each guarantees safety.
What does the CAP theorem actually say, and what are the common misreadings of it?
When should a system choose leaderless replication, and what consistency risks does it bring?
Explain consistent hashing and why virtual nodes are used.
Why is two-phase commit a blocking protocol, and how do Spanner and CockroachDB work around that?
How do vector clocks detect concurrent writes, and what problem do hybrid logical clocks solve?
Compare LSM trees and B-trees for a write-heavy workload.
What are quorum reads and writes, and when does W + R > N fail to guarantee a fresh read?
How does Cassandra combine ideas from Dynamo and Bigtable?
What is TrueTime and how does Spanner use it to get external consistency?
How does eventual consistency differ from causal consistency, and which anomalies does each allow?
What are sagas and what do they give up compared to distributed transactions?
How do gossip protocols and failure detectors keep cluster membership up to date?
What throughput, in transactions per second, does Raft achieve on commodity hardware?
